stages.name: soil_preparation
stages.objective: Create fine puddle, incorporate organic matter, level field
actions: Plough field 2-3 times with tractor/cultivator to 15-20 cm depth
Apply well-decomposed FYM or compost at 10-12 t/acre
Flood field and puddle with 2-3 passes of puddler/country plough
Level field using laser leveler or wooden plank for uniform water depth
Repair bunds and channels to prevent water leakage
Apply basal fertilizer mix (DAP or SSP) before final puddling
sustainable_alternatives: Replace 50% inorganic P with rock phosphate (cost saving ~₹200/acre)
Incorporate dhaincha green manure 45 days before transplanting (saves ~₹1500/acre on FYM)
Use no-till DSR to eliminate puddling (saves ₹2700/acre)

common_issues.symptoms: Uneven water, hard pan not broken

common_issues.remedy_cost_effective: Level with laser and provide drainage channel

key_tips: Puddling depth 15-20 cm ensures soft bed for roots
Apply P fertilizer based on soil test to avoid fixation
Incorporate green manure at flowering stage for best N contribution

stages.name: nursery_raising
actions: Select high-yielding, disease-tolerant variety (e.g., Rajendra Mahsuri-1, Sahbhagi Dhan)
Seed treatment with carbendazim 2g/kg seed or Trichoderma 4g/kg
Prepare raised nursery beds 10 m x 1.25 m with fine tilth
Sow pre-germinated seeds at 4-5 kg per 100 m² area
Apply seedling stage nutrients: 200g DAP + 100g MOP per bed
Irrigate daily, maintain thin film of water after 1 week
Spray 0.2% ZnSO₄ + 0.5% urea at 12-15 days for green color
Harden seedlings by gradual water withdrawal 5 days before uprooting
sustainable_alternatives: Use SRI mat nursery (saves seed 90%, cost ~₹100/acre)
Treat with neem oil 3 ml/kg seed for pest prevention (cost ~₹15/acre)
Apply vermicompost in nursery bed instead of chemical DAP (cost ~₹150/acre)

common_issues.remedy_cost_effective: Reduce seed rate, increase light exposure

key_tips: Use 25-day-old seedlings for transplanting; older seedlings tiller less
Nursery area should be 1/10th of main field
Raise nursery on high ground to avoid waterlogging

stages.name: transplanting
stages.objective: Establish uniform stand with optimum density
actions: Transplant 1-2 seedlings per hill (SRI) to 2-3 (conventional) at 20x15 cm spacing
Maintain 2-3 cm water depth during transplanting for weed suppression
Gap filling at 5-7 days after transplanting (DAT)
Apply first top-dressing of urea (if basal not given) at 7 DAT
sustainable_alternatives: Direct seeded rice (DSR): eliminate transplanting entirely (saves ₹3000/acre)
SRI with single seedling 25x25 cm (saves labor, increases yield potential)
Mechanical transplanting (rent ~₹1200/acre, reduces labor)
key_tips: Transplant in afternoon to reduce shock
Use rope marker for uniform spacing
SRI: adopt cono-weeding after 10 days

stages.name: vegetative
stages.objective: Promote rapid canopy development and root establishment
actions: Apply second dose of urea (35 kg/acre) at active tillering (20-25 DAT)
Maintain 3-5 cm water level consistently
Conoweeding/ hand weeding at 10-15 DAT and 25-30 DAT
Monitor for stem borer and leaf folder
Apply zinc sulphate 10 kg/acre if deficiency appears
Spray neem oil 5ml/l as prophylactic
sustainable_alternatives: LCC-based N application (saves 20-30% urea, ₹100/acre)
Incorporate Azolla (20 q/acre) as green manure for N
Use pheromone traps for stem borer (5 traps/acre, ₹100)

common_issues.remedy_cost_effective: Conoweed twice, apply bispyribac sodium 10% SC @ 200ml/acre

key_tips: AWD irrigation: irrigate when water drops 15 cm below soil surface
Install bird perches (7/acre) for insect control
Split top-dress urea into 2 applications to avoid lodging

stages.name: tillering
actions: Maintain shallow water (2-3 cm) to encourage tillering
Weed management: cultural/ mechanical, avoid herbicide stress
Apply 3rd urea dose (if needed) @ 18 kg/acre at panicle initiation start
Foliar spray of 2% DAP + 1% K to boost tillers
sustainable_alternatives: Curd churning effluent (buttermilk) spray for growth promoters (cost ~₹50/acre)
Apply Jeevamrit (5% solution) to stimulate microbial activity

common_issues.remedy_cost_effective: Drain water to reduce N uptake

key_tips: Target 15-20 productive tillers/hill for good yield
Avoid standing water >5 cm after maximum tillering to control unproductive tillers

stages.name: panicle_initiation
stages.objective: Ensure proper panicle development and spikelet formation
actions: Maintain 3-5 cm water level (critical stage for water)
Apply K (MOP 20 kg/acre) to improve panicle strength
Spray boron (0.2% Borax) to prevent panicle sterility
Scout for sheath blight and BPH
Avoid any water stress during booting
sustainable_alternatives: Use wood ash as K source (50 kg/acre, cost ~₹100)
Apply seaweed extract (2ml/l) for micronutrients (₹150/acre)
key_tips: Boron application improves grain filling
This stage is most sensitive to water stress; keep sufficient water
Avoid nitrogen at this stage to prevent lodging

stages.name: flowering
stages.objective: Achieve high pollination rate and spikelet fertility
actions: Maintain 2-3 cm water to ensure humidity
Avoid pesticide sprays that harm pollinators (morning hours)
Apply foliar spray of 0.5% urea + 0.2% boron if weather is dry
Monitor for false smut and gundhi bug
sustainable_alternatives: Flower visitor conservation: avoid all insecticides for 2 weeks
Use fish amino acid spray (2ml/l) as biostimulant

common_issues.organic_option: No effective organic control; prevent by avoiding excess N

common_issues.symptoms: Brown spots on grain, foul smell

key_tips: Flowering usually occurs 25-30 days after panicle initiation
After 50% flowering, gradually reduce water
Do not apply granulated pesticides during flowering

stages.name: grain_filling
stages.objective: Maximize grain size, weight, and quality
actions: Maintain moist soil, not submerged (intermittent wetting)
Apply last micronutrient spray (Zn + B 0.2%) if delayed
Monitor for leaf folder and RTV (virus) vectors
Install bird perching poles
Drain water 10-15 days before harvest
sustainable_alternatives: Use vermiwash (5ml/l) for nutrient enrichment
Strategic irrigation with AWD (saves water, no cost change)

common_issues.remedy_cost_effective: Harvest early at 22% moisture, dry mechanically

key_tips: Stop irrigation when 80% grains are in hard dough stage
Check moisture by biting grain; if it breaks clean, it's ready
Yellowing of lower leaves is normal; do not add N

stages.name: maturity_harvest
stages.objective: Harvest at right moisture with minimal losses
actions: Harvest when 80% panicles golden yellow and moisture 20-22%
Use sickles or reaper to cut at ground level
Thresh immediately or within 24 hours
Clean grain with winnowing fan
Sun-dry to 14% moisture (thickness feels crisp)
sustainable_alternatives: Hand threshing (labor intensive, zero fuel cost)
Use pedal-operated thresher (rent ~₹200/acre)

common_issues.remedy_cost_effective: Harvest early, thresh and dry fast

key_tips: Harvest in morning to minimize shattering
Do not stack wet crop for long to avoid heat damage
Use tarpaulin during threshing to reduce rodent access

stages.name: post_harvest_storage
stages.objective: Store paddy safely, preserve quality for MSP/market
actions: Dry grain to 12-14% moisture (sun-dry or mechanical dryer)
Clean grain, remove broken grains and foreign matter
Fumigate storage area with aluminum phosphide (expert only) or neem leaves
Store in jute/ HDPE bags on wooden pallets, away from walls
Monitor for moisture and pests every 15 days
sustainable_alternatives: Store with dried neem leaves as insect repellent (cost ₹50)
Use metal silo (long-term, zero chemical)
key_tips: Store grain only after moisture <14%
Keep separate from old stock to avoid cross infestation
If selling for MSP, ensure moisture <=17% (varies by state) or face deductions

pest_calendar.prevention: Seed treatment with carbendazim or Trichoderma

pest_calendar.watch_for: Brown oval spots with yellow halo
Water-soaked lesions, yellowing from leaf tip
pest_calendar.prevention: Avoid excess N, use resistant varieties

pest_calendar.watch_for: Water-soaked oval lesions on leaf sheath
pest_calendar.prevention: Reduce plant density, avoid heavy N
Use resistant vars, avoid excessive N
Maintain open canopy, avoid thick planting
Avoid excess N, especially at booting

pest_calendar.watch_for: Brown spots on grains, foul smell

pest_calendar.remedy_cost_effective: Control green leafhopper vector with imidacloprid
pest_calendar.organic_option: Remove diseased plants, use barrier crops

sustainable_practices: IPM with pheromone traps and biological control
Leaf color chart (LCC) for need-based N
Laser land leveling for water uniformity

tools_and_machinery.name: Conoweeder
tools_and_machinery.use: Weed control and soil aeration in SRI/transplanted rice

storage_guidance.short_term_method: Sun-dried, store in jute bags with neem leaves on wooden pallets
storage_guidance.long_term_method: Dried to 12% moisture, store in metal silo or fumigated warehouse
storage_guidance.storage_pest_prevention: Mix 2 kg neem powder per quintal, maintain cleanliness and aeration

post_harvest_value_addition: Rice bran oil extraction from husk
Branding and packaging for local markets
